Maladaptive Strategies.value: wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed

Memory.value: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together

Negative Appraisals.value: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed

vignette: Kamal's eyes would scan the room before he'd take a seat, his gaze lingering on each face as if searching for potential threats. This hypervigilance had become second nature to him since that fateful night when his partner of five years, Amir, turned violent. It was a darkness Kamal couldn't shake off, one that seeped into every aspect of his life. The memory of the attack still echoed in his mind like a scream. He recalled the sound of helicopters outside their apartment building as Amir's hands closed around his throat. The noise had been deafening then; now it was a trigger that sent Kamal spiraling back to that night. Anytime he heard a helicopter or an aircraft, he'd feel his heart racing, his palms growing sweaty, and his mind replaying the terror. Kamal had come to believe that the world was no longer a safe place, that danger lurked in every corner. His community organizing work, once a source of pride and purpose, now felt like a liability. He'd catch himself scanning crowds for potential threats, always on the lookout for someone who might hurt him again. This constant vigilance left him exhausted but unable to relax. After the attack, Kamal had found it impossible to return to their shared apartment. The physical location held too many painful memories, and he couldn't bear the thought of setting foot in that space again. Instead, he'd moved into a new place on the other side of town, one with more natural light and less reminders of Amir. Kamal had also developed a habit of wearing concealing clothing - baggy shirts, loose pants, and a hat to cover his face. It was as if he wanted to disappear from view, to avoid being noticed by anyone who might pose a threat. This need for concealment extended beyond his attire; Kamal found himself avoiding social gatherings and community events, places where he'd once thrived. When memories of the attack surfaced, they came in fragmented pieces - a snatch of Amir's voice, the feel of his fingers closing around Kamal's wrist, or the sound of those helicopters. These disconnected recollections left Kamal feeling disoriented and lost, like he was trying to piece together a puzzle with missing parts. As time passed, Kamal became increasingly withdrawn. He felt betrayed not only by Amir but also by himself; in his mind, the abuse had happened because of some fundamental flaw within him. His self-blame echoed through every waking moment: "I should have seen it coming," or "I must be weak to have let this happen." These thoughts eroded Kamal's sense of identity and purpose. Kamal's relationship with his new partner, Rachel, suffered as a result. She'd try to reassure him that he was safe now, that she loved him for who he was, but Kamal couldn't shake off the feeling of being broken. He felt like he was living in a world where the rules no longer applied, where violence and betrayal lurked around every corner. The darkness - both literal and metaphorical - had become Kamal's constant companion. It seeped into his dreams, his waking hours, and even his relationships. What frightened him most was losing himself completely to this darkness, becoming a shadow of the man he once was. The thought sent shivers down his spine. Kamal finally sought help when Rachel convinced him that their relationship couldn't survive under the weight of his unspoken pain. As he sat in the therapist's office, Kamal felt a glimmer of hope - perhaps there was a way to rebuild himself, to rediscover the man he'd been before Amir's abuse shattered his world. But for now, the memories lingered, and the darkness remained.
